newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN METALS - ZINC PREMIUMS FALL ON SLOW DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN METALS - ZINC PREMIUMS FALL ON SLOW DEMAND.

text.p: Taiwan's spot zinc premiums fell sharply to US$60-80 per tonne from US$120-150 a week ago due to sluggish local demand, Taipei metals traders said on Tuesday.
"Suppliers are cutting their zinc premiums by about half," a Taipei-based U.S. metal dealer said. "Taiwan's zinc market is still sluggish and suppliers are cutting prices to make deals."
Traders said summer has been slow season for Taiwan's zinc market.
The recent rally and high volatility on the London Metal Exchange's zinc market further dampened Taiwan's demand as most buyers were sidelined, traders said.
"The zinc market is too volatile right now," a trader said. "Buyers are waiting for the market to consolidate a bit."
Traders said there were talks that Chinese suppliers have delayed or cancelled some zinc shipments to Taiwan, but only about 2,000 tonnes were confirmed.
"Some Chinese zinc shipments to Taiwan were cancelled or delayed, but those only totalled about 2,000 tonnes" a Taiwan metal trader said.
Traders said Taiwan's major zinc buyers, in general, are reluctant to source zinc from China due to its poor quality and less reliable delivery schedules.
Taiwan traders said Chinese suppliers recently offered lower quality zinc at US$1,550 a tonne, but no deal was reported.
